claims.text: Uncertainty quantification in free-form LLM responses is challenging due to the difficulty of defining task-specific uncertainties such as semantics.
Bayesian decision theory can address uncertainty quantification by assuming utility is characterized by a similarity measure between generated and hypothetical true responses.
Similarity-based utility assumptions enable principled quantification of a model's subjective uncertainty.
Similarity-based utility assumptions enable principled calibration of a model's subjective uncertainty.
Epistemic uncertainty can be derived based on a missing data perspective.
Epistemic uncertainty can be characterized as an excess risk.
The proposed uncertainty quantification methods are applicable to black-box language models.
Epistemic uncertainty offers a promising deferral strategy for efficient data acquisition in in-context learning.

evidence.description: Experiments on question answering and machine translation tasks demonstrate that epistemic uncertainty is effective for data acquisition deferral.

methodologies.name: Bayesian Decision Theory Uncertainty Framework
methodologies.description: A framework for quantifying subjective and epistemic uncertainty in NLG using similarity measures as utility functions.

limitations.text: Identifying task-specific uncertainties (e.g., about semantics) appears difficult to define in general cases.
